summary: SDK exponential backoff synchronicity exposes rate-window queueing as apparent inference regression
description:
Issue summary:
BrightDocs reported intermittent long tail latency and increased client-side timeouts during sustained concurrent inference calls. Initial symptom reported as "slow model responses" and streaming stalls for a subset of requests.

Impact:
- Multiple production routes for BrightDocs saw 10-20% of requests exceed customer-side timeouts during peak; perceived as model slowdown.
- Customer observed spike in aborted requests and increased error rates in their metrics (up to +18% 5xx/timeout during the window).
- Affects dedicated pool in us-east-1.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (dedicated GPU pool, BrightDocs tenant)
- prod | us-east-1
- SDK versions in use: brightdocs-app@v2.6.0 and brightdocs-batcher@v1.2.3 (internal SDK derived from open-source SDK).
- Serving runtime: rwinf-2026-02-14 build

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) From a client with SDK configured with base_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=2s, jitter disabled (SDK v1.2.3 default for high-throughput configs).
2) Ramp to 200 concurrent short-text generation requests (prompt length ~40 tokens) sustained for 5 minutes targeting the BrightDocs route.
3) Observe request latency distribution and error codes.

Observed behavior:
- At steady-state a periodic ~60s burst pattern emerges: 429s spike for ~2-6s, immediately followed by a long tail of requests which appear to hang (client perceives timeouts) for up to 8-12s.
- Server logs show rate-window enforcement queuing behavior (router logs: "enqueued in window shard=17 length=120"), then a short windowed flush returning 429s.
- Client traces show synchronized retry attempts (many retries aligned within the same 200-500ms due to exponential backoff without randomized jitter) which amplifies the queueing and extends the visible latency.
- No model inference CPU/GPU throttling observed; GPU utilization remains normal. Kernel-level traces show per-tenant request queue depth rising during the period.

Initial analysis / hypothesis:
- The combination of per-tenant rate-window enforcement (server-side windowing at 1s resolution) and deterministic exponential backoff in the customer's SDK caused retries to align, producing short 429 bursts and amplified queueing at the window boundary.
- Result is perceived inference regression even though token generation path and kernel latency are unchanged.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Enable SDK client jitter immediately (workaround steps provided in chat).
- Reduce concurrency from 200 -> 80 for critical routes until server-side mitigation is deployed.
- Customer applied SDK change and reported immediate drop in observed timeouts (preliminary).

Resolution plan (server + SDK):
1) Short-term (hotfix): Deploy SDK patch that enables randomized jitter by default for v1.2.x branch (PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/442). Target rollout 2026-03-16.
2) Server-side smoothing: Implement per-tenant smoothing buffer in rate-window handler to avoid flush spikes (ticket created in infra backlog). Canary in us-east-1, then full rollout.
3) Observability: Add a tenant-level metric for window-flush size and a high-resolution retry correlation trace map.
4) Postmortem and runbook update to include guidance on SDK backoff settings vs dedicated pool windowing.

Follow-ups:
- Infra to track PR #1289 for smoothing and schedule canary: Owner: Priya Desai, ETA 2026-03-18.
- SDK team to merge jitter default: Owner: Erik Johnson, ETA 2026-03-16.
- CS to coordinate BrightDocs test window after canary: Owner: Lina Moreno, tentative 2026-03-19.

Resolution notes (in progress):
- Customer accepted temporary workaround. SDK jitter patch validated in integration tests. Server smoothing feature is in design and will be canaried next week.
